title: Ants at a tree trunk: does going round it read right?
question: One of these lets an ant work its way round a trunk (a pause as long as the trunk is thick, then it appears on the far side); the other turns it away. Does the pause read as going round, or as a glitch?
context_md: Your design: 'they basically just teleport to the other side with a delay long enough for however thick the trunk is, so they don't actually overlap with the cells ever.' The animal never enters the wood -- that is what makes it safe, since occupying a stem stops it counting as the plant's anchor and empties a lab bed. On the real wooded world (scene=colony seed 1, 12,000 frames, one binary, CROSS_TRUNK=0 for the control): blocked steps 15.7% -> 7.3%, tissue blocking 656 -> 216, 243 crossings begun and 243 completed with none abandoned, and limb severing 3,987 -> 3,770, so plants are slightly better off. What still blocks is trunks with no far side to come out on -- inside a crown, or into open air with no foothold -- which is the rule declining rather than a gap. The question is only whether the pause LOOKS like going round.
